The skill that makes skills.

Every skill in this repo carries the same freight: press branding, a
forge-verified CI caller, a marketplace entry, a required check, a
`skill-invariants.json`, a baseline eval. `CLAUDE.md` documents adding one as a
**ten-step manual checklist** — and every step of it is invisible when skipped.
`ci / shipflow` gated nothing on `main` from the day it was introduced because
one of those steps was done by hand and half-done.

smith does the ten steps in one command, and spends the saved attention on the
part that decides whether a skill is any good: its one rule, the line between
what code decides and what the model decides, and a real run frozen as its
baseline.

**A skill is done when a real run of it is frozen in its evals — not when the
files exist.** The scaffolded baseline test *fails* until that run happens, so
`ci / <name>` cannot go green on a skill nobody has run.

```bash
smith detect                                  # every registry, as one table
smith check-spec --spec tally.spec.json       # graded harder than CI, while it is still free
smith scaffold  --spec tally.spec.json        # the tree + all seven wiring points
smith freeze --skill tally --from ./run --command "…" --trap-command "…"
smith verify --skill tally                    # the ladder, and which rung you reached
```

Install via the [claude-skills marketplace](https://github.com/natejswenson/claude-skills).
